title: Discontinuation of Update Support for Existing Perpetual Licenses
content:
![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/98273b7564f64196ae9539146ba2e8dd/images/a9a53fe8465446b8ae0484cb4bbda69adefault_thumbnail.jpg)As announced, we would like to remind you that the update support to **Marvelous Designer 12** will be discontinued after following the new release of Marvelous Designer 2024.0 (scheduled for the end of February) 

[**NOTICE: License Policy**](https://www.marvelousdesigner.com/discover/news/view/54)[**Change**](https://connect.clo-set.com/community/post/4e9be626237843789ff8a2d019244a26)[**(2020)**](https://www.marvelousdesigner.com/discover/news/view/54)**  
**

To ensure a seamless transition and not miss the opportunity to update to version 12, we will extend the purchase period until 7 days after the release of version 2024.0.

**Ends on March 6th 2024 (0:00 PT)**

# **New Features in Marvelous Designer 12**

# **Community's Most Voted TOP 5 New Features**

  * [Retopology Improvements](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QZ7WkPPItE8)

  * [Roll Up](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ou9eQlbQsHU)

  * [Auto Create Fitting Suit](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Gq0RfMnAwX4)

  * [USD File Compatibility](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O6tmEmzjG7E)

  * [Animation Editor Improvements](https://youtu.be/HMPyCmeUkIo?feature=shared)




For more features, refer to the [manual](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/en-us/articles/12196570463129-Marvelous-Designer-12-12-1-12-2-New-Feature-List).

# **How To Proceed Version Update**

Follow a simple procedure to purchase the version update.

Purchase the version update to 12 through the 'Dashboard' on the Marvelous Designer website.

Alternatively, you can purchase directly via the following links (login required):

  * **Personal License Holder:**[**https://marvelousdesigner.com/pricing/per/option/year**](https://marvelousdesigner.com/pricing/per/option/year)

  * **Enterprise License Holder:**[**https://marvelousdesigner.com/pricing/ent/option/year**](https://marvelousdesigner.com/pricing/ent/option/year)




If you are eligible for update/trade-in purchase, "START NOW" button will appear in the dashboard.

![9465f7612e874ac1a64a608a2a654aed](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/98273b7564f64196ae9539146ba2e8dd/images/9465f7612e874ac1a64a608a2a654aede56128a025ff40a984ca1383b3332ea9.jpg)

# **Update Purchase Available Period**

You can continue to purchase an update to Marvelous Designer 12 Perpetual, 7 days after Marvelous Designer version 2024.0 is released (the exact date will be sent as a notification via email)

After this period, updates for perpetual licenses will no longer be available.

# **THINGS TO KNOW**

**Q1. Can I continue using my perpetual license even after the update purchase support is discontinued?**

Yes, you can continue using your perpetual license. However, technical support could be limited according to the software support policy. The level of support may vary depending on the version and product. For more details, check the [Marvelous Designer support policy.](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/en-us/articles/18375639754137-Marvelous-Designer-Support-Policy-Supported-Product-Versions)

### 

**Q2. What is the difference between version update and trade-in?**

  * Version Update: You can update your perpetual license to version 12 while you maintain your other perpetual license. 

  * Trade-in: You are able to exchange your existing perpetual license through a "Trade-in" option for a 1 year subscription (for personal users) OR 2 year subscription (for enterprise users). After you receive either the 1 year or 2 year subscription depending on your user type, you will no longer have access to your Perpetual license. During the period of subscription, all users will be guaranteed to the latest version of the software without any additional charges or fees.




** Note: The eligibility criteria and prices are the same for both version update and trade-in.

### 

**Q3.   If I update my perpetual license to version 12 Perpetual, can I purchase an update to version 2024.0?**

No, purchasing updates for perpetual licenses are only available up to Marvelous Designer 12. Any releases after Marvelous Designer 12, are not eligible for purchase. Marvelous Designer 2024.0 will be subscription only.

### 

**Q4. Can I use versions 12.1/12.2 with updating to version 12?**

Yes, you can use all versions -12/12.1/12.2 

### 

**Q5. I own a perpetual license and want to use version 2024.0. What should I do?**

We will recommend a trade-in purchase option for you. Trade-in option will have you give up your perpetual license for a subscription license type (the period of subscription will depend on your license type, see below). Subscription type license will allow you to have the most up to date version of Marvelous Designer during the duration of subscription.

  * For individual users (Personal): Your Perpetual License → Convert to 1 Year Subscription License 

  * For company/academic users (Enterprise/Academic): Your Perpetual License → Convert to 2 Year Subscription License (per copy) 




### 

**Q6. I have a perpetual license version 8 or lower. Can I update to version 12?  **

If your current perpetual license corresponds to versions 9, 10, or 11, you can either select a 'Version Update' or opt for 'Trade-In' However, if you have version 8 or lower, updating to version 12 is not possible.

**Q7. Does this policy apply to both personal and enterprise licenses?**

Yes, these changes apply to both personal and enterprise licenses.

# **Contact us and Support**

If you have any questions or concerns regarding the discontinuation of perpetual license updates after 12, please feel free to contact our [support team](https://www.marvelousdesigner.com/support/contact).

We appreciate your continued support and promise to provide you with better services going forward.

Thank you.

Marvelous Designer Support Team.
content_description: This webpage serves to inform users about the upcoming discontinuation of support for Marvelous Designer 12, provide details on the transition to Marvelous Designer 2024, and outline the purchasing options available for updates.

title: The Antique
content:
## _Eugene shares the behind-the-scenes story of Marvelous Designer's involvement in her short animation, "The Antique"_

* * *

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/950ac101ff9c40a9a235593b0103b866/images/2ee5f69a338c4c14ad4a991e587fc203%ED%99%94%EB%A9%B4%20%EC%BA%A1%EC%B2%98%202024-12-10%20180831.png)

<https://vimeo.com/823293011>

# **Artist Introduction**

Hi, my name is Eugene Jung - working as a 3D motion graphics designer. I have a desire to create character animations myself, so I'm consistently studying and working on character-related projects personally.

# **Tell us about the animation project: The Antique.**

"The Antique" is a short animation depicting 'Yeon,' who operates a vintage goods store, preparing for the store's opening. I started the production with the idea of creating a video filled with things I like. The work aims to portray vintage items, a warm sunny atmosphere, and relaxing morning hours.

# **We'd like to hear more about the art direction in the costume of Yeon. What was the visual style you were aiming for?**

I envisioned the season within "The Antique" transitioning from winter to spring. Throughout the video, I aimed for a casual yet warm feeling in the chosen clothing that complements the sunlight coming through the windows. I wanted the attire to be comfortable yet convey a sense of intimacy. Therefore, I ultimately opted for a cardigan and jeans in the video, incorporating bright spring colors to create a fresh and lively atmosphere.

# **Why did you decide to use Marvelous Designer? How did it help you serve in your animation project?**

I believe that expressing the natural movement of hair and clothing plays a key in conveying the vitality of a character, so I pay close attention to this aspect when working. In the case of "The Antique," where the character takes center stage, achieving a natural flow in the clothing movement was important. Utilizing Marvelous Designer allowed me to depict the natural movement of the clothing, enabling me to effectively capture the vitality of the character as I envisioned throughout the entire video.

# **Can you give us a quick overview of the different tools used in your pipeline including Marvelous Designer?**

# [Planning]

I collect references for tone, mood, the protagonist's appearance, and clothing. I then organize the storyline in written form. Based on the script, I create storyboards and produce style frames for essential scenes in the video. During this process, I use Marvelous Designer to test the feel of the clothing.

# [Video Editing]

After roughing out the major movements of the camera and characters in 3D, I proceed to overall video editing. Once I confirm that the video length and composition are seamless, I delve into detailed animation.

# [Cloth Simulation]

Upon completion of the animation, I import the character into Marvelous Designer to simulate the clothing. The costumes created in Marvelous Designer are further refined in Substance Painter to craft intricate clothing textures.

# [Finalizing]

After final adjustments to the look, I proceed to render, composite, and edit the background music, concluding the video production process.

# **Could you give examples of some of the iconic scenes and characters Marvelous Designer has been used for in “The Antique”?**

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/950ac101ff9c40a9a235593b0103b866/images/04c97dee5ad04aaa9cce20c436a6c616a005090f2f31422fa2fbf5ede4e1fd0b%20%281%29.png)

Here are the initial scenes featuring Yeon, the first being the panoramic shot and the subsequent mirror scene. The panoramic scene reveals Yeon's full body, and it was crucial to simulate the clothing's natural movement as she walks. In the mirror scene, Marvelous Designer was used for the floral-patterned curtains, lace on the shelf, and the moving curtains reflected in the mirror, as well as the tablecloth.

With Marvelous Designer, I could achieve a natural movement for the curtains swaying in the wind and the tablecloth, enhancing the overall realism of these scenes.

# **Are there any tips and tricks with Marvelous Designer that you can share with the community?**

I tend to purchase project files from the Marvelous Designer Asset Store (CONNECT) and external markets (such as ArtStation) when needed, and I use them after making adjustments to fit the characters.

In this project as well, I bought a project file, modified it to suit the character, and incorporated it into the workflow.

By taking a reference to how other designers create patterns and sew using Marvelous Designer, I've been able to enhance my understanding of the software. It provides valuable insights into different approaches and techniques employed by fellow designers, contributing to an overall improvement in my proficiency with Marvelous Designer.

# **How can you describe your overall experience of the use of the Marvelous Designer?**

Marvelous Designer allows for the quick production of high-quality garments within a short period. Not only that, but it also makes it very easy to achieve a realistic feel of fabric. Additionally, there is a wealth of tutorials and both free and paid items available for users, making it quite accessible even for those unfamiliar with Marvelous Designer. This enables users to easily utilize only the necessary features, even without extensive knowledge of the software.

[Link to Behance](https://www.behance.net/withorwithout)

[Link to Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/withorwithoutx/)
content_description: Discover how Eugene Jung utilized Marvelous Designer to bring the character and vibrant atmosphere of her short animation, "The Antique," to life through innovative costume design and realistic fabric movement.

title: Making An Armor In Marvelous Designer: Breaking Boundaries
content:
## _Meet Sarah, a skilled 3D designer, as she unveils her process for crafting hard-surface armor using Marvelous Designer. The hard surface look is seamlessly achieved within the creative realm of Marvelous Designer._

* * *

# **Interview with Sarah Prado | Armor Creation in MD | 3D artist**

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/8d4b3d81d36b4b1f976cbfb3db7a3342/images/30efa36ca78444c980c8506dcd6a44dd2733c7e3de954fbcb3d558d99ff94578.png)

# **Artist Introduction.**

My name is Sarah, I am a Brazilian 3D Artist, Fashion Designer, gamer, and mother of cats. I have a university degree in Fashion and for more than 10 years I worked as a designer, patternmaker, and seamstress in local industries, mainly with bridal gowns and formal wear for women.

I had my first experience with Marvelous in 2020 during the Covid lockdown, which has blown my mind. Since then I have fully migrated to 3D, where I can work with more fantastic designs and test patterns for much less expense and much less waste.

Nowadays I use mainly Marvelous, Substance Painter, and Blender.

Although one can apply Marvelous into to a range of areas such as home decor and stylized characters, I really enjoy working with realistic but fantastic designs.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/8d4b3d81d36b4b1f976cbfb3db7a3342/images/47381740a2d046839a26fbfdfbe2add5sorceress%20isometric.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/8d4b3d81d36b4b1f976cbfb3db7a3342/images/76f1edc7c11b4a318b0bb57004547425cathedral%20render3-front2.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/8d4b3d81d36b4b1f976cbfb3db7a3342/images/3200103c62c24e228272db1d2e6a67ddcathedral%20render3-back2.png)

# **You've recently released impressive armor creations that have received a tremendous response from the user community. We are extremely curious to know what inspired you to implement armor creation that can be created on hard surfaces in other software. Can you tell us more?﻿**

﻿This artwork in particular came from this annoying situation that older gamer girls would face when playing RPG and fantasy genre when the armor supposed to protect the character's body is actually more like a bikini made of steel and sheer fabric. So I made a meme-like expectation vs reality artwork. It was fun and I enjoyed how both versions ended up, but I put much more time and research into the realistic one.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/8d4b3d81d36b4b1f976cbfb3db7a3342/images/1fdd42fb51714dae9d01020023fa6842expectation%20x%20reality2.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/8d4b3d81d36b4b1f976cbfb3db7a3342/images/9b3ec971b5014c318e0dd64919e59938armor%20ref.png)

# **What was your primary focus in your artwork? What are the powerful benefits of making armor using Marvelous Designer?**

It is kind of a personal challenge since I was told I could nor should do any of the sort in clothing simulation software. So I've been playing with adding hard-surface elements totally made into Marvelous in previous artworks before the armor with great results even when simulating animation and the main reason for that is: I'm a total noob in other programs.

As a fashion designer, I guess I'm more functional thinking in clothing patterns than as a sculptor. I have no idea if a blacksmith would use cut pieces of flat metal to bend and weld into armor, but that's definitely what I would do. I think that's what cosplay makers do, anyway.

So, why not? People come from different backgrounds and I think we all should be allowed to go after the results we want no matter the tool we are more comfortable with!

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/8d4b3d81d36b4b1f976cbfb3db7a3342/images/f02d686156544563a2db50a39230c4faarmor%20marvelous.png)

# **Would you be able to provide us with an overview of your pipeline, focusing on Marvelous Designer? Have you encountered any challenges and how have you overcome them?**

Of course! It's basically a fabric with stiffer but smooth aspect presets (high shear, high bending, medium stretch, etc) and fold angles.

I like starting with an avatar in A-pose, where I make a doublet: a regular fabric garment usually worn under the armor. I keep it single-layered since most of the reverse won't be shown, the sewn lines are actually internal lines with fold angles over 180.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/8d4b3d81d36b4b1f976cbfb3db7a3342/images/7715e9b907d244d5a7da85066f035733step1.png)

Then I add the patterns to be the armor itself, I like to start with a Trim Full Grain Leather fabric and then tweak its properties until it reaches the desired hardness.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/8d4b3d81d36b4b1f976cbfb3db7a3342/images/8c308fd6f361446aad510aa61916fefastep2.png)

To keep the armor pieces attached one to another I use internal lines to emulate rivets or links. I may model some leather stripes to attach the metal pieces too. It will serve as a guide later when texturing to make it look like a rivet.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/8d4b3d81d36b4b1f976cbfb3db7a3342/images/f06bc6ff50fd437ebfb81e5387a193e7step3.png)

  
That done, I go to designing the surface angles using internal lines and changing the fold angles too, <180 for the pinch effect and >180 for creases. Some designs will need several internal lines and different fold angles. It may be needed to apply fold angles on the sewing lines too. That's what will make the sculpted appearance of the metal plates. Fold angles only show in 3D when simulating in "normal" or "fitting" modes, "fast" mode does not deliver a good result.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/8d4b3d81d36b4b1f976cbfb3db7a3342/images/424f8901080b49eab71c0421e1342b2fstep4.png)

Depending on the piece, it also should be necessary to apply bond or seam tapings ("under the collar" preset is great for this) and, after reaching the desired shape, solidify so it stays in place.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/8d4b3d81d36b4b1f976cbfb3db7a3342/images/769a5db341de4247b5134d5a12bf02a0step5.png)

Last but not least, I like to play with the thickness too. Usually, I lower the curved side geometry or even remove it to keep it more angular.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/8d4b3d81d36b4b1f976cbfb3db7a3342/images/ac61a436bc224a6cb8df73e186c81f44step6.png)

  
That's the essence of how I make armor and hard-surface elements using Marvelous!

The only challenge I faced was that I had to adapt the patterns to visually fit what I wanted.

For example, the cords that fasten the vambraces were not really long cords but little pieces sewn in the right places; the buckles were not really buckles but hard fabric cut in the right shapes. It doesn't need to be, just needs to look like it is. Anything else just required patience and creativity to shape the design.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/8d4b3d81d36b4b1f976cbfb3db7a3342/images/f468b275282443648dc65289f82ee263step7.png)

  


# **Are there any tips and tricks with Marvelous Designer that you can share with the community?**

There's one I like: for some pieces when you need to have a gap, for example, a corset backside or a deep neckline you want to keep in place, just make a piece of pattern fitting the gap and sew to the piece borders, then when simulating it will not show any pressure points or deformations. Deactivate (pattern only) and hide the 3D view of this pattern. You'll then have a gap with straight borders and the hidden piece will not be exported with your object!

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/8d4b3d81d36b4b1f976cbfb3db7a3342/images/82ef2d9ff83f4a2a953e3dbb5a7a499dtip%20final.png)

If you need to simulate an animation then you'll have to activate it, but it may face some instabilities then. Testing is the key.

# **by Sarah Prado**

[Link to Artstation](https://www.artstation.com/sandorah)

## UPP reveals the spacecraft production techniques   
from the movie "Voyagers". Marvelous Designer played a crucial role in crafting realistic spaceships.

* * *

# **Interview with UPP | Voyager | VFX Studio**

# **Could you introduce your studio?**

UPP is an international VFX and Post Production Studio. Since its establishment in 1994, UPP has become one of the largest and most versatile Visual Effects and Post Production Houses in Mainland Europe. With teams in Prague and Budapest, we work with filmmakers and clients from all over the world.

# **Could you briefly introduce the project: Voyagers?**

The Voyagers Project is about a crew of astronauts on a multi-generational mission descending into paranoia and madness, unable to determine what is real and what isn't.

Directed by: Neil Burger

Produced by: Basil Iwanyk, Neil Burger, Brendon Boyea

Stars: Colin Farrell, Tye Sheridan, Fionn Whitehead and Lily-Rose Depp

# **Can you explain how Marvelous Designer was used for the spacesuit and its impact on this project?**

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b665ad057db742da859c503f444622aa/images/8847c06992974840a2af9e4ec7339e3eezgif-1-9b2343fb57.webp)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b665ad057db742da859c503f444622aa/images/351a094442c4488f97362fe39aed2691ezgif-1-5e02c636c0.webp)

When we created the spacesuit in a bag for the Voyager project, we based it on a photogrammetric scan.We created the spacesuit in a bag in individual layers.

Our goal was to approach the production as efficiently as possible, therefore we produced the entire asset, except for small details, in Marvelous Designer.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b665ad057db742da859c503f444622aa/images/cfe5933821034cda8b9e41ea4a44a4c5UPP_2.webp)

# **Apart from the spacesuit, which other objects were created using Marvelous Designer?**

We also used Marvelous Designer to easily create the fabric covering the spaceship's hull.

Below we will present a series of images that present step-by-step how the cloth pieces were created for a specific piece that is part of the spaceship.

  * **Collision model of the structure under the cloth - Creation of basic parts of the cloth - UV layout of the basic cloth parts**


![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b665ad057db742da859c503f444622aa/images/44a60eead4c746ad91f2dd7246724b48ssClothA_md_01_objectForDynamics.webp)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b665ad057db742da859c503f444622aa/images/5dd8c92a97fd4c09b85687bb99007e75ssClothA_md_02_partsCreated.webp)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b665ad057db742da859c503f444622aa/images/04e1971e47a142ff95e6555ca4edeafessClothA_md_03_partsUVs.webp)

  * **Stitching of individual basic cloth parts with basic sewing parameter settings - First simulation of the cloth to get the basic shape**


![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b665ad057db742da859c503f444622aa/images/f53f6027aa3e4dd88f0f6793fa570887ssClothA_md_04_segmentsSewing.webp)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b665ad057db742da859c503f444622aa/images/d560b220a6c44358bc68a2cd6479446bssClothA_md_05_firstSim.webp)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b665ad057db742da859c503f444622aa/images/9f5d3f94ed444e09b0effb38ae166943ssClothA_md_06_firstSim.webp)

  * **Adjusting the pressure parameter to obtain a better shape - Simulation with the cloth pinned to the construction - Extra cloth parts added to the edges of the construction (The extra cloth tubes give us a better shape)**


![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b665ad057db742da859c503f444622aa/images/dd81684c70794478881b27a5d635caf9ssClothA_md_07_pressureAdded.webp)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b665ad057db742da859c503f444622aa/images/f67f96b7bed944fa970b32945e988e69ssClothA_md_09_pinResult.webp)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b665ad057db742da859c503f444622aa/images/f464f33ca44d4205a745fa6c50b3b125ssClothA_md_10_tubesAdded.webp)

  * **Simulation with the extra cloth tubes-UV layout of the basic cloth parts with extra cloth tubes**


![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b665ad057db742da859c503f444622aa/images/962d2dd194fd4a1d869ffcb014aae3f1ssClothA_md_11_tubesAdded.webp)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b665ad057db742da859c503f444622aa/images/f1a7b7dbc89b400296a203f941ee1c65ssClothA_md_12_tubesAdded.webp)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b665ad057db742da859c503f444622aa/images/98077b030ed14a9e80a3d6103e2b6f55ssClothA_md_13_tubesAdded.webp)

  * **The following images show the final results before and after rendering.**


![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b665ad057db742da859c503f444622aa/images/141bb4ef559e4de9b98943fb3ad85989ssClothA_render_01_parts.webp)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b665ad057db742da859c503f444622aa/images/d40ea1ce8e8a416da9bf3a2571cf3fc3ssClothA_render_02_final.webp)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b665ad057db742da859c503f444622aa/images/455f341ab4a64a13b4ae3c78406e8b7dssClothA_render_03_final.webp)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b665ad057db742da859c503f444622aa/images/59de367220c54002b23af91b95814069ssClothB_render_01_parts.webp)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b665ad057db742da859c503f444622aa/images/1b0116d15b45446194d91b27865b1ec3ssClothB_render_02_wireframe.webp)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b665ad057db742da859c503f444622aa/images/a2e72571fa634c739a4a398890ea6e76ssClothB_render_03_shade.webp)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b665ad057db742da859c503f444622aa/images/40469ff1419c433ab8f2aa6787603a92ssClothB_render_04_final.webp)

**CLO Virtual Fashion** , an industry leader in cloth simulation technology, is thrilled to announce that Marvelous Designer - the company's 3D design software for film, gaming and VFX artists - and Founder Jaden Oh have been awarded the Scientific and Engineering Award from the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences. 

The annual Scientific and Technical Awards celebrate the achievements that demonstrate a proven record of contributing significant value to the process of making motion pictures. Marvelous Designer has been credited with creating "a pattern-based approach to digital costume construction, unifying design and visualization and providing a virtual analogy to physical tailoring."

The Academy noted that under the guidance of Founder Jaden Oh, "the team of engineers, UX designers and 3D designers at CLO Virtual Fashion has helped to raise the quality of appearance and motion in digital wardrobe creations."

Jaden Oh, Founder, CLO Virtual Fashion: "We are deeply honored to receive the Academy Award for Marvelous Designer. This recognition is a testament to the hard work, dedication, and innovation of our team. To all the filmmakers, animators and designers who selected Marvelous Designer as your tool of choice to bring your stories to life on the big screen: thank you."

Among the many films that have utilized Marvelous Designer are “Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness”, “Avengers: Infinity War”, “The Boss Baby: Family Business”, “The Hobbit: The Unexpected Journey”, “John Wick: Chapter 3 - Parabellum”, “Mulan”, “Fantastic Beasts: The Crimes of Grindelwald”, “Moana”, “The Adventures of Tintin”, “Avatar: Way of Water”, “Spider-Man: Into the Spider-verse.”

The Scientific-Technical Awards ceremony will be held Friday, February 23, at the Academy Museum of Motion Pictures in Los Angeles.

Evolved from the word "clothing", CLO Virtual Fashion's mission is to empower everything related to garments - from design to styling, and beyond. With more than 20 years of research and development in accurate garment simulation, we are leading the market by digitally creating, merging, and converging all components related to digital garments through our state-of-the-art 3D cloth simulation algorithm. 

From 3D garment design software, digital asset management and design development collaborative platform, to consumer facing services such as virtual fitting on e-commerce, all of CLO Virtual Fashion's products and services are interconnected to provide users with a more consolidated experience.

title: Assassin's Creed Mirage: Cinematic World Premiere
content:
## _Digic Pictures, working on Assassin's Creed Mirage, relies on Marvelous Designer for intricate character clothing, emphasizing its speed, detail, and ease of use._

* * *

# **Could you introduce the recent project - Assassin's Creed Mirage?**

**Tamás Varga (character supervisor):**

We are very pleased that Ubisoft has chosen Digic again for the trailer of the latest Assassin's Creed game.

Mirage takes the series back to its roots, with a renewed emphasis on stealth, parkour, and assassination, and a solid narrative-driven campaign set mainly within a single historical city, Baghdad 9th Century. Baghdad was the center of the Caliphate during the Golden Age of Islam. It was perhaps the greatest cultural, commercial,l and scientific center of the world at the time - and it is here that the protagonist, the street thief Basim, meets the Assassin Order.

So, as well as the main characters, it was also very important to portray the city and its inhabitants as vividly as possible, as a kind of living backdrop to the story of the protagonist's coming of age.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/c53e93f6b83e451ca99efbb7051de231/images/26de2c7e74a440d188700e380ae9fe62image9.png)

# **How is Marvelous Designer integrated in the project pipeline?**

**Tamás Varga (character supervisor):**

We have been using Marvelous Designer for a long time and by now we are well aware of its capabilities, so we knew from the beginning that we would rely heavily on this software to implement the characters.

The clothing for the main characters (assassins, guards, etc.) was extremely complex: overlapping layers of different fabrics and armor, tight-fitting garments, and baggy capes - all things that Marvelous Designer was clearly the solution for.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/c53e93f6b83e451ca99efbb7051de231/images/f8ed48cb2b9c4d2fae743223ca5cdb21image7.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/c53e93f6b83e451ca99efbb7051de231/images/0eb3610985264d8ca00a680f9f8d82b9image8.png)

But we also knew in advance that our characters would be moving through the Baghdad crowd throughout, that they would be surrounded by these "extra" characters (plain extras in English) in a lot of scenes, and that our director wanted to highlight some of these citizens. So it was decided very early on that all the other characters' outfits in the film would be made in Marvelous Designer, and simulated in every shot.

This required a number of major improvements, but luckily in many cases, we had been working on each of these for years and this became our first project where all the pieces of the puzzle finally fell into place.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/c53e93f6b83e451ca99efbb7051de231/images/13cca107f32240bfa1adb729273a0029image1.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/c53e93f6b83e451ca99efbb7051de231/images/a904848b24e54ec9addc634460e043c4Image2.png)

**Zoltán Turkovich (CFX lead):**

From the modeling phase to the final simulation, the work on the suits was done in Marvelous Designer, on the CFX side, the finalization of the simulations was done only in 3rd party software.

Due to the large amount of assets and varied mass in the project, we developed a script called AutoSim tool, which after the final body animations on the Background characters were done, automatically ran the Marvelous Designer cloth simulations with default settings and saved them directly to the rendered shots, saving a lot of manual work on the project.

The rendered garment on hero assets is usually just driven by the simulated Marvelous Designer garment in our pipeline, but on this project, also due to the large amount of variation on the Background characters, the raw Marvelous Designer geometries were uploaded and rendered.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/c53e93f6b83e451ca99efbb7051de231/images/5690caa425ee452eb2550d9138bd9428Image5.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/c53e93f6b83e451ca99efbb7051de231/images/3c52859b4413460f84df51a6d5057f57image6.png)

# **Please let me know what is the strength of Marvelous Designer compared to other simulation tools.**

**Varga Tamás (character supervisor):**

The most important strength of Marvelous Designer is that it can simulate extremely beautiful and detailed clothing, and very quickly.

It is also a big advantage that it can be used for asset production. In a lot of the shots in the film, we rendered the background characters one by one with models made in Marvelous Designer.

**Zoltán Turkovich (CFX lead):**

Sample-based modeling, due to the clothing setup, it is easy to achieve authentic, realistic clothing simulations. The software is very easy to learn, it has a simple learning curve, so even novice CFX artists can learn it quickly. When the body animations are properly set up for clothing simulation, the clothing simulations run very stable, allowing easy clothing simulation of large amounts of characters.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/c53e93f6b83e451ca99efbb7051de231/images/14d6297efd5942e09c29ef796574f775Image3.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/c53e93f6b83e451ca99efbb7051de231/images/6dad3315471c4e7ca56d878777944480Image4.png)

# **Could you give examples of some of the iconic scenes and characters Marvelous Designer has been used for?**

**Zoltán Turkovich (CFX lead):**

To me the most iconic sequence is the depiction of the Baghdadi bazaar and bazaar crowd, with lots of clothing variations, and colors - really achieved the look and feel of a live and vibrant market.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/c53e93f6b83e451ca99efbb7051de231/images/2c5717e8e35d4ceca497be74342761ddimage10.png)

CFX-wise, the hood-turban removal of the initiation ceremony was a challenge to keep the costume simulation authentic with heavy contact animation.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/c53e93f6b83e451ca99efbb7051de231/images/5c081b74856f49ebaa4a4ac880fbd828image11.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/c53e93f6b83e451ca99efbb7051de231/images/10528ef55d954652aa066482eb4888cdimage12.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/c53e93f6b83e451ca99efbb7051de231/images/5c5022287c8a4590a0d19ed436bfe068image15.png)

# **If you could give advice to a person who just started to work with Marvelous Designer, what would it be?**

**Edina Schmidt (Modeling Artist)**

Get a powerful processor, learn basic pattern editing. Recommend trying to model your own clothes first!

**Norbert Geresdi (Modeling Artist)**

Keep it simple! Although it's an exciting challenge to realize a well-drawn concept, it's usually a lot of work. Customizing even the simplest looking garments can be super challenging, so it's worth studying classic patterns first.

**József Sáfár (CFX artist)**

Expect post-simulation post-production and have fun!

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/c53e93f6b83e451ca99efbb7051de231/images/a2821212a7894df7b2b9f04ce306d637image13.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/c53e93f6b83e451ca99efbb7051de231/images/4f2bd44ecca74b7b80ca2c705565f373image14.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/c53e93f6b83e451ca99efbb7051de231/images/c29756bc4cc1452b95fb9bcda467ed24image16.png)
content_description: Explore how Digic Pictures leverages Marvelous Designer to create intricate and realistic character clothing for Assassin's Creed Mirage, enhancing the game's vibrant historical setting and character depth.

title: Meet Our New Logo
content:
![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/bb3b875dd5154ade98ae61dd768de63d/images/de4d8b1ed2954b45b08a875b11ad139cdefault_thumbnail.jpg)

Have you noticed that our logo has changed? Some of you may have already known about the update, but many of you might not have! 

# **It’s official: introducing the new logo for Marvelous Designer!**

![ab7ed97af4444a8fab96c45684795691](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/bb3b875dd5154ade98ae61dd768de63d/images/ab7ed97af4444a8fab96c45684795691bi_before.jpg)

The Marvelous Designer logo has experienced several updates since its initial launch to modernize its appearance in line with functional advancements and reflect the product's identity.

A significant transformation occurred in 2019 from the original logo, resulting in the recognizable cube-shaped design.

In 2023, we solidified the new Marvelous Designer logo with a new identity and direction that we are actively steering forward.

We’d like to tell you more about how the new logo was developed and why we made the update.

# **Behind our logo makeover**

![843000c009eb4b6fb47101dfd717255c](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/bb3b875dd5154ade98ae61dd768de63d/images/843000c009eb4b6fb47101dfd717255clogo_sketch.jpg)

**What was the reason for the logo rebranding?**

We started to recognize that the time was right for us to demonstrate that we have a bigger value to our users while keeping the essence of our offering.

While our previous brand identity centered on “3D garment simulation”,

the new logo adds diversity and depth to highlight a new vision for the software - a boundary-breaking creation tool. 

# **Boundary-breaking creation tool**

![11fecf72849140ce863c21b853cca719](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/bb3b875dd5154ade98ae61dd768de63d/images/11fecf72849140ce863c21b853cca719breaking%20boundry.jpg) Through this rebranding, we aim to present not just a simple change but to communicate the direction and values of Marvelous Designer.

The new logo for Marvelous Designer, ‘Marvelous Strip’ takes inspiration from ‘Möbius strip’, visualizing the concept ‘Boundary Breaking Garment’ that dissolves boundaries with our users.  


This represents the simultaneous coexistence of our users and us, the beginning and end, the front and back, the inside and outside of the fabric.

By doing so, it goes beyond breaking the fixed notions of creators, showcasing the diverse possibilities where Marvelous Designer's technology can be utilized.  


As an example of the diverse possibilities, Marvelous Designer can be utilized as a creation tool not only for garment production but also for various purposes such as accessories, vinyl, and even things like fish. This signifies that Marvelous Designer can be applied in a broader range of industries beyond the gaming, VFX, animation, and film sectors, including fashion, content creation, art, architecture, interior design, manufacturing, education, and the metaverse industry.

In line with our primary objectives, we will strive to enhance features that are most widely needed for our users to support the seamless workflow in the gaming, VFX, and animation fields.

# **Introducing a new release name with the new logo  **

In November 2023, there was an update to version 12.2, which included new features, particularly beneficial for game development production, and received positive feedback from our user community!

Now, you might be curious about when the release of the next major version is planned and what interesting features it will include. Let me address each of your curiosities.

Firstly, the release of the major version is scheduled for 2024.

Additionally, this new version will be introduced with a refreshed version name.

Until now, Marvelous Designer versions were sequentially numbered behind the name "Marvelous Designer.”

However, starting from 2024, the versioning will utilize the release year as part of the version name, making it easier for users to identify the progressively enhanced Marvelous Designer each year.

# **What’s we’re excited for**

In Marvelous Designer 2024, you can expect to see new features focused on Production Optimization.

That will include the introduction of automatic retopology, improvements to patch retopology, animation video capture functionality, Unreal Engine Plug-in, and more!

![f192d6fcdb0340159a6670ae1359d25c](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/bb3b875dd5154ade98ae61dd768de63d/images/f192d6fcdb0340159a6670ae1359d25capplication.jpg)

title: Design Miyacore: Exclusive Winner Interview
content:
## _Alison, Grand Award winner in the Design MIYACORE Contest, shares her journey as a 3D artist, blending historical elegance with modern flair using Marvelous Designer._

* * *

The Design MIYACORE contest, held from September to October this year, has successfully concluded.

Presented in collaboration with the CONNECT asset store for Marvelous Designer and SUNMIYA CLUB, this special event brought vibrancy to the community through the inventive spirit and enthusiasm of its participants.

Notably, a Marvelous Designer user received the GRAND AWARD, garnering significant attention.

To delve deeper into this exceptional work, we're excited to share an interview with the GRAND AWARD winner, ALISON GADELETA, with all of you. Let's explore her creative world together!

# **Interview with ALISON GADALETA | 3D Artist**

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/7e113424ee7e492c98594150ac035fc5/images/307a822f09ff4b158d0a9b212acb8f0a6ee6f7abea1949d6b36ae5fb5884282d.png)

# **Artist Introduction: please tell us about yourself.**

Hi everyone! My name is Alison, I am an Italian 3D Artist specializing in Virtual Fashion. I'm currently working in a fashion company as a 3D Design Specialist for almost one year.

I started using Marvelous Designer when I was pursuing my Master’s Degree in computer graphics in 2021 that’s where my real passion was born.

It was during this time that I delved into Maya, ZBrush, Substance Painter, and, of course, Marvelous Designer.

Being passionate about computer graphics and 3d in general, it was a lot of fun to participate in this contest and use these beautiful characters to create the outfit.

# **We’d like to hear more about the art direction in your Design MIYACORE Contest. What was the visual style you were aiming for?**

Before we started modeling, each of us could choose two themes from those proposed: Juicy Newtro and Bad Lady.

The Bad Lady theme was much closer to my style, and I could have had many more style options, but I deliberately chose the other theme so that I could step out of my comfort zone and create an outfit that was different, but at the same time reflected my personality.

Also, Juice Newtro was a perfect theme to challenge myself on the color scheme.

I started by creating a concept board from random references about clothing in America in the 1950’s. I researched what was fashionable in those years and what were the main characteristics a woman in the 50’s looked for in an outfit.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/7e113424ee7e492c98594150ac035fc5/images/e0d75187d0284f87bebe72808ae96acd96961aafb8f54d25be83dad1e53cd10b.png)

During my research, I was fascinated by one of America's most beloved first ladies: Jacqueline Lee Kennedy, wife of the President of USA John Fitzgerald Kennedy. A woman with a strong determination, a mix of charm and elegance. In fact, her style was inspiring for the creation of this project.

The result is the creation of an elegant and playful cocktail dress that highlights the hourglass silhouette, typical of that time.

To add a modern touch, I wanted to create the dress shorter than standard, also to balance the overall volume.

Another key element within the design is the outerwear: a raincoat with voluminous sleeves with contrasting lining made of silk to enhance the interior and make it a luxurious garment.

Finally, to add particularity to the look I added the scarf in tone with the dress, a belt to match the shoes, and a pearl necklace same as the buttons on the dress.

# **Would you be able to give us a quick overview of the different tools you use in your pipeline with a focus on Marvelous Designer? Have you encountered any challenges and how have you overcome them?**

I think it is only through experience that each of us learns to have our own workflow.

The first phase during my process of creating any dress is the blocking phase. In this phase I create the general volumes and build the basic 2D pattern, enhancing it according to the avatar's body. In addition, I add the buttons but do not insert any additional details.

At this stage, the avatar is in A-pose.

In the intermediate stage, I begin to pose the avatar and create more detail in the clothes I have modeled; I change the thicknesses of the pieces, increase the resolution of the garments, and set the materials to see if they are suitable for that type of dress.

Only when I'm satisfied with the look, then I move onto the detailing stage paying attention to draping, because it is very important for realistic modeling. To finish, I create accessories such as shoes, scarf, necklaces, and belts. In order not to overload the simulation, I usually create separate files for each of these elements and finally add them to the main file.

I textured everything in Marvelous Designer and rendered with V-Ray, while I used Photoshop for post-production.

This was my first time modeling shoes in Marvelous Designer. It was challenging but if you remember to freeze each piece step by step when you are satisfied, everything becomes much easier!

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/7e113424ee7e492c98594150ac035fc5/images/4c7fd59dbe0b4c4dbe13fee7e80942dadba8ad959b8e44cf8af3669f983be313.png)

# **Are there any tips and tricks with Marvelous Designer that you can share with the community?**

One tip I would like to share is to pay close attention to the details, looking at an existing physical garment figuring out what components and materials are used in its creation, and try to replicate it in a realistic way.

For example, let us dwell on the inside of the coat: it has different materials and components: facing, lining, and made of nylon and silk, respectively.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/7e113424ee7e492c98594150ac035fc5/images/63515571715f4035be3b3b0e7d66a01f8e056c323a9a4b53a069cb4e8e614f06.png)

A trick I use in creating models that have multiple layers is the layer clone option.

To make the simulation more stable, I usually higher the particle distance and set everything in strengthen.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/7e113424ee7e492c98594150ac035fc5/images/885f81585d694904a34c911250fae3d056dc29233fb74e0b99bee91a8229b1c4.png)

After creating the layer underneath, I lock the simulation and, when selecting, use the remove linked editing tool.

Then I can draw internal lines and cut and sew the interior as I prefer to create facing and lining.

Another trick: in reality the lining is a little larger than the outer, so I increase the shrinkage settings in warp and weft.

Finally, I check the material, remove the strengthened mode, lower the particle distance again, and simulate again for a more realistic drape.

title: PROJECT: SHIN RAMYUN
content:
## _Gryun Kim, an Emmy-awarded Motion Graphic Designer, creatively utilizes Marvelous Designer for realistic ramen packaging._

* * *

# **Artist introduction**

Hello, I'm Gryun Kim, and I work as a Motion Graphic Designer. Currently, I'm based in Los Angeles and primarily focus on creating Title Sequences and TV commercial film projects. My most recent work, "The Last of Us Main Title," received an Emmy Awards nomination. I've also had the opportunity to work on other notable projects, including title sequences for "Men in Black," DC's "Doom Patrol," and HBO's "His Dark Materials." Furthermore, I have experience in conducting seminars at events such as Motion Plus Design, NAB 2022, and Siggraph. Additionally, I am active as an NFT artist on the renowned platform Superrare and have participated in several interviews discussing NFTs across various media outlets. Most recently, I had the privilege of showcasing my NFT artwork at the 2022 LA Art Fair.

#   
**Tell us about the project : Shin Ramen  **

The Shin Ramyun Project developed gradually by responding to questions about 'how to make noodles' from the Cinema4D user group. Initially, it started by creating examples of making noodles, but it eventually expanded into a project by developing packaging and even simulating the boiling process. Since I began working on my personal project, I aimed to make the most of this opportunity. I also considered delving into skills such as Marvelous Designer, UV, and 3D painting, which I had been eager to learn. Moreover, I cannot overlook the fact that, thanks to this project, I had the chance to showcase 'Shin Ramen' at the Maxon Booth during the recent Siggraph event.

# **It's very interesting to see that you used Marvelous Designer to create the ramen package. How did you decide to use Marvelous Designer for this part and how did it help your project?**

Whenever I create realistic works, I approach the “process” with the idea of incorporating creativity into it. I consider the process as an integral part of the artwork.

For instance, when I imagined a ramen package, I investigated the actual process of creating a ramen package and thought it would be fun to replicate the same process. So, I started by making the noodle texture first just like in real production. Then, I used pressure and sewing functions in Marvelous Designer to wrap the paper printed to match the noodle texture around it, gradually decreasing its size with pressure from the top and bottom to create the package in the shape of ramen. I believed that this process could be faithfully reproduced in Marvelous Designer.

Marvelous Designer's sewing and pressure features made it easy to create the ramen package that wraps around the noodles, and since Marvelous Designer starts with 2D pattern design, it was straightforward to create the UV maps as a bonus. Thanks to this, I was able to significantly save time. Furthermore, I used the **Pin** function to add more details and wrinkles to the ramen bag.

# **Can you give us a quick overview of the different tools used in your pipeline?**

The ramen production is divided into two volumes: Vol.1, which covers package completion, and Vol.2, which focuses on the boiling presentation.

In Vol.1, the process involves 

1) Noodle modeling (Cinema 4D)

2) Package design (Marvelous Designer)

3) Package tearing (Cinema 4D)

4) Rendering done using Octane Render.

In Vol.2, it begins 

1) Pot modeling (Cinema 4D) 

2) UV (RizomUV) 

3) Painting (Substance Painter) 

4) Decorative materials captured through photography and Cinema 4D. 

5) Bubbles and broth effects (Cinema 4D)

# **Are there any other projects where you used Marvelous Designer in unconventional ways like the example of the ramen package?**

I have utilized Marvelous Designer extensively in my personal artwork. In particular, I utilized Marvelous Designer for the vinyl effects in [my personal project](https://www.behance.net/gallery/69730571/HR-GIGER-\(Personal-Work\)). 

I also used Marvelous Designer for vinyl effects, creating bandates in my work for DC's "Doom Patrol”.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/d854bc8857904b9ead4762a2f952a593/images/d079b5dd9935408ab1df2a44d73bf30fDOOMPATROL_2_20231110_02.jpg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/d854bc8857904b9ead4762a2f952a593/images/31af4363205a4ac1866487e58fbb84e5DOOMPATROL_3_20231110_03.jpg)

I also used Marvelous Designer in creating the American flag for "The Swamp Main Title" project.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/d854bc8857904b9ead4762a2f952a593/images/da6e3a5d19d1408b8e9bc45969d8b428DOOMPATROL_6_20231110_04.jpg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/d854bc8857904b9ead4762a2f952a593/images/07f33fbaafdc4c1b8681b10525f0a71bTHESWAMP_1_20231110_01.png)

# **Are there any tips and tricks with Marvelous Designer that you can share with the community as a 3D Motion Graphic Designer?  **

Marvelous Designer offers incredibly fast GPU simulations, allowing for detailed fabric representation. However, it can sometimes result in heavy file sizes when used for motion graphics. As a tip and trick, I utilize detailed wrinkles created with Marvelous Designer by baking them as textures and then apply them as normal or bump maps. This approach helps me bring in detailed textures without overloading the scene with individual wrinkle meshes, allowing for smooth and efficient work.

# **How can you describe your overall experience of the use of the Marvelous Designer?**

Marvelous Designer has been of tremendous assistance to me in achieving realistic fabric textures. Its real-time feedback and fast simulation speed are especially valuable, enabling me to explore various possibilities in my work efficiently. Additionally, the use of **Pin** and **Sewing** functions has provided me with the flexibility to create diverse effects, which has proven to be a significant advantage. I look forward to continuing my artistic endeavors using Marvelous Designer in the future.

title: S.KOREA IN THE 1980s
content:
## _WoonJu, a 3D artist, explores 1980s South Korea nostalgia, leveraging Marvelous Designer for fabric-rich scenes and recommending its versatile use._

* * *

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/1aae5490bf774cc894b72a45ba61ae08/images/5a08490f7b544fe6a191deeeaa73266e299baef861b441b1974646ec99405b76.png)

# **Artist introduction**

Hello. My name is WoonJu and I'm studying 3D backgrounds. I majored in fine art western painting, focusing on landscape paintings, and became interested in 3D, which led me to create this project.

# **What inspired you to come up with this concept of the project?**

The concept of the project is 1980s South Korea, which encompasses my parents' teens and twenties. 

I had warm feelings for my parents when they were in their teens and twenties in the 1980s, and even though I didn't live through that era, I feel nostalgic when I look at their faded photos.

My parents often tell me stories about their youth, and how they used to pass the time listening to the radio with their favorite DJs, and when their favorite songs came on the radio, they would record them and listen to them.

As a gift to my parents, who still remember that era, I wanted to make them feel like they were in a time machine.

I was also influenced by a Korean drama called Reply 1988 that I was watching at the time, so I thought it would be fun to create a 3D background that was set in that era.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/1aae5490bf774cc894b72a45ba61ae08/images/102cb975069c4154a9c6d1c1f340435b3165630573a54f4f9d6e7df9b3769e75.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/1aae5490bf774cc894b72a45ba61ae08/images/24c4d2b06545474abdc796d93c1be781911db59b729542a8b508747eecc09f72.png)

# **Which corners that you want to highlight in this artwork? How did Marvelous Designer help to serve?**

This is my first project, but I've always wanted to dabble with different 3D tools, so I wanted to be able to approach any object I made in different ways.

By the end of the project, I wanted to be able to create anything and not be intimidated by it, and I wanted to be someone who could model and texture beautifully.

I used Marvelous Designer for this piece for the bed, curtains, sofa, tablecloth, carpeting, yellow floor mattress, and more.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/1aae5490bf774cc894b72a45ba61ae08/images/0dd06e6609a3471bb96f1e75ce653e8e2126ba6670bf413ba05f388b2388cafd.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/1aae5490bf774cc894b72a45ba61ae08/images/a8da08f5aff842219fdc2162c35c9a88975a8aa08f7140f0aa6f2e8a9182877f.png)

# **What are some of the feature usage that you would like to recommend while working on the background art?  **

The Marvelous Designer is a great tool to use for creating things that involve clothes in your everyday life.

To create the basic foundation of the fabric, I used Marvelous Designer to create high and low 3D models, which I then transferred to the 3D Model tool to clean up. 

The advantage of Marvelous Designer over other modeling tools is that you can pull out everything about the fabric, the texture of the fabric, the orientation of the fabric, the bulge of the fabric, etc. in real-time.

I think Marvelous Designer is the only program that can give you the best cloth quality while reducing production time.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/1aae5490bf774cc894b72a45ba61ae08/images/f15ea5e55b3b412095e6e980a4d33135b530b0de1c43477c9122dc3cafe84fde.jpg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/1aae5490bf774cc894b72a45ba61ae08/images/5907e0e2a0e547a58d24c399517ae3f9ba9b855b43024cc5ac2add81f68ef5cf.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/1aae5490bf774cc894b72a45ba61ae08/images/df4ce7e4b9834053a865634d381f9c4c811f99b3eff64898896d53e409c8d44c.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/1aae5490bf774cc894b72a45ba61ae08/images/78ef47b7ae6f4bbdb37e6462c7c80256e81be747f72145d1881bea77aaf28c72.png)

# **Are there any tips and tricks with Marvelous Designer that you can share with the community?**

I mentioned earlier that we create high and low 3D models within Marvelous Designer, and the Particle Distance and Remesh are useful for this. 

Particle Distance allows you to adjust the number of faces based on a number, which I used to create the high mesh. 

Remesh allows you to replace triangular faces with square faces, which is useful for creating a low mesh.

# **How would you recommend Marvelous Designer to the background artist who has never used the solution?  **

I've only completed projects that fit the basic concept of "Marvelous Designer is for cloth," but I think it can be used to create things that don't involve cloth, with a focus on real-time rendering.

For example, I used Marvelous Designer to create rubber gloves, a kitchen staple. 

Marvelous Designer is a tool for 3D modelers to make modeling easier in any way possible. I want to encourage 3D background modelers to think outside the box and utilize Marvelous Designer's ability to render in real-time within a background.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/1aae5490bf774cc894b72a45ba61ae08/images/2627d99bcfc045d5871926be8256e125131381cbe9c94f278d2fb92047b14718.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/1aae5490bf774cc894b72a45ba61ae08/images/7c02f822039940d2bb91224aeb836eff4564e1ce4cf9481cb7e175747296b61e.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/1aae5490bf774cc894b72a45ba61ae08/images/538d9ecd8fa14ea49ac6c736ee0b871304402ddf112c4b37b6dbf2249632f687.jpg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/1aae5490bf774cc894b72a45ba61ae08/images/e3e086274492446b9227d1d2761d23a2c3bc43b535e643c2b1d61ae5f6d2c8a2.png)

title: WHEN DIGITIAL MEETS TRADITIONAL
content:
## _AMC Studio collaborates with La Blouse Roumaine, blending tradition with tech. Marvelous Designer aids precise garment recreation, enriching cultural storytelling._

* * *

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/5383d8a9399848079442b6724fce3a1e/images/6e63bfc67ff744928073dbcecd68d67020231017_01.jpg)

# **Studio Introduction**

AMC Studio is an art studio offering digital art creation (3D, 2D, and Concept Art), content solutions, and technical tools for the gaming industry. Our incredibly skilled and passionate team of artists creates top quality art and offers production services for a broad range of project types. We’ve partnered with great names in the industry and helped shape some of the most acclaimed titles, such as: Dead Space Remake, The Witcher 3, Marvel’s Spider-Man, Call of Duty franchise, World of Tanks, Mafia Definitive Edition & more.

# **What project do you want to present to us?**

The project we are about to present is a collaboration between 2 realms: the traditional and the digital. We worked alongside La Blouse Roumaine, a non-governmental organization that promotes Romanian folklore, tradition and culture. The project’s objective was to recreate a few traditional costumes from different parts of Romania.

We had to do a lot of research and work with scientific consultants to make sure we recreated the costumes as authentically as possible. All colors and geometric shapes have a particular meaning, the position and the way the ornaments are placed is also very important. So we had to make sure we got everything right.

# **When do you start using Marvelous Designer on your costumes?**

The first step before jumping into the actual work is to gather the references. In this particular case, some were researched by us and then discussed with the embroidery consultants. Some came from books or museum archives, and some were provided by our partners in the project. You can see a few of the references we gathered for each costume that helped guide us in our process.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/5383d8a9399848079442b6724fce3a1e/images/4ef41a924eed4e0f871d743f87f8704320231017_02.png)

The next step is to create a blockout that helps us see the bigger volumes and establish the general proportions. In this case, we chose to start the blockout directly in Marvelous Designer, because we decided it would be best suited to help us see some quick realistic fold simulations. It was also very important for us to capture the materiality of the garments from the beginning, so the variety of material presets really helped in this endeavor.

Some settings that we found very useful are Shrinkage Weft and Shrinkage Warp. That’s because they allowed us to change the proportions of the garment on the horizontal and vertical axis without actually changing the 2D pattern, which is a non-destructive workflow, and it saves a lot of time. Working with layers is also very handy, and we used them in creating our vest. We needed it to have a stiffer feel while also having some folds that we could control easier, so we found this to be the best approach.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/5383d8a9399848079442b6724fce3a1e/images/104e66518f604fe0975f842b8ac064d120231017_03.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/5383d8a9399848079442b6724fce3a1e/images/13629b7fad6c498cbcf9defc59872ece20231017_04.png)

#   
**What are the long-term benefits of using Marvelous Designer?**

When we were happy with the results we had in Marvelous, we prepared the garments for export one by one. First, we lower the particle distance if needed, to get the maximum amount of details.

After that, we quadrangulate or remesh the garment and we export it with the following settings: single object, unwelded, thin and unified UV coordinates on. Usually, we export with unwelded points, but it’s not a rule. It depends on how you approach the garment later.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/5383d8a9399848079442b6724fce3a1e/images/cc6bcd9bdf1848f49ab52fe71e2b6f6020231017_05.png)

We reset the 2D arrangement and export the pattern so we can later use it in Maya.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/5383d8a9399848079442b6724fce3a1e/images/03f8d4ddaf4a4d2882589bc432e56e9520231017_06.png)

After that, we import the 2D pattern in ZBrush and ZRemesh them to have a cleaner, sculptable topology. A tip here is to go quite low with the geometry resolution because it's easier to control. Keep in mind that you now have the initial 2D pattern from Marvelous and another zremeshed version of it.

The next step is to go to Maya and import the 3D garment and 2D pattern initially exported from Marvelous Designer, and also the ZRemeshed 2D. Make sure you match the contour of the remeshed 2D pattern with the one from Marvelous.

You can now transfer the UV's from the 2D pattern in Marvelous Designer to your ZRemeshed pattern.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/5383d8a9399848079442b6724fce3a1e/images/5e8571f6bf224d308bbf15d9e002df2420231017_07.png)

The same operation will be made to transfer the attributes from the 3D garment to your 2D remeshed pattern, though some settings differ.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/5383d8a9399848079442b6724fce3a1e/images/332999dc60614716be2d86c78eab018520231017_08.png)

Now you will have a clean geometry with UV’s to work with. We transfer back to ZBrush and start adding thickness with Panel Loops.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/5383d8a9399848079442b6724fce3a1e/images/3ec9f88aabd2457797260c0a90aa5c3d20231017_09.png)

We again use the initial 3D garment form Marvelous to re-project all the details on the newly cleaned geometry using **morph target**  on each subdivision created. That’s so we can easily clean all the imperfections that might appear during this process with the **morph brush**. As you can see, using Marvelous helps us a great deal along the way. Not only to achieve believable and fast folds but also on the technical side, giving us the possibility to extract really nice UV’s as well.

# **How was your pattern making process and did you encounter any challenges?**

After having a good base to start from, we begin to add all the necessary details. For this project we needed to be very precise in creating all our ornaments and symbols because they all have stories to tell. The costume as a whole tells you which part of the country the person wearing it comes from, sometimes down to a particular street in a village, what sort of celebration it’s worn for, whether the person wearing it is young or elderly. Woven in the fabric are also some traditional protective charms. All in all, our traditional costumes are like wearable temples.

So taking everything into account, it was crucial for us to recreate in 3D all the details as closely to the references as possible.

Something that we really focused on was the creation of the ornate patterns, which we worked on using different methods. One of the methods starts with creating the pattern in ZBrush, making sure it's tileable, assigning polypaint (for ID color if needed), making an imm brush to help with the placement and then either using it for the final baking stage, or creating a displacement from it.

IMM brushes

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/5383d8a9399848079442b6724fce3a1e/images/3d04ec2d93264b378db62a09ad56058b20231017_10.png)

Planning the displacement map

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/5383d8a9399848079442b6724fce3a1e/images/6be5a599f1ba4e1fbcdcb010e5fb6d4720231017_11.png)

Selection of patterns created in ZBrush.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/5383d8a9399848079442b6724fce3a1e/images/d4278b4a48814b8ebd66cdbd593efef620231017_12.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/5383d8a9399848079442b6724fce3a1e/images/e291c275b01f4cae99e7d1852ca7d8db20231017_13.png)

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/5383d8a9399848079442b6724fce3a1e/images/cd1886f8f85e41bf895b48dcbb9bdbcf20231017_14.png)

Another method used was to create masks that helped us achieve different results for materials, such as leather. There was a lot of testing done in Photoshop and ZBrush to make sure we achieved the proportions and distribution needed with each pattern.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/5383d8a9399848079442b6724fce3a1e/images/1f5b4bf0d7a74cd7be9b378d2b892a5c20231017_15.png)

We also did the patterns by first creating a color map that was used as an ID map in Substance Painter to generate the desired pattern. This worked only with square looking embroideries.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/5383d8a9399848079442b6724fce3a1e/images/49bedc51aa724c2abd718ace78f4b04220231017_16.png)

title: RECAP: SIGGRAPH 2023 + MEET-UP EVENT in LA
content:
What an exciting August it has been for us! But before the memories settle, we are delighted to share a quick recap of our presence in Los Angeles in early August. 

* * *

# **SIGGRAPH 2023 EXHIBITION (August 8th-10th 2023)  
**

For the very first time, Marvelous Designer x CLO, as a unified entity within CLO Virtual Fashion, jointly hosted a booth, where we successfully introduced our *eCLOsystem, encompassing all of our software and platforms. We had the privilege of engaging with numerous industry leaders, artists and students during the conference.  


_*_[ **_CLO VIRTUAL FASHION’_**](https://www.clovirtualfashion.com/) _S  eCLOsystem_

 _By touching each and every step of the journey of a garment, we envision our technology and solutions to create a new ecosystem to bring countless benefits to the industry. Building efficient and sustainable workflow, reducing production time and cost, enabling higher accuracy and quality, we believe our solutions are leading the innovation to bring the world where every real garment is tagged to a virtual garment, and vice versa._

# ![8478a1b3dcf74aaab334ddaf0531c9aa](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/e9f115628645436a809e29971069a4d9/images/8478a1b3dcf74aaab334ddaf0531c9aa2023-08-08_SIGGRAPH_SC_183602.jpg)**MARVELOUS DESIGNER & CLO - A GREAT SYNERGY! **

We listened to their experiences and shared insights about our upcoming updates that can help enhance workflows. Beyond conventional demonstrations centered on costumes, we also introduced the expansive scope of Marvelous Designer's potential, which encompassed the creation of various items such as bat wings, seaweed, and koi fish. 

Furthermore, it's important not to overlook the significant advantage of having two distinct demo stations – one exclusively for Marvelous Designer and the other for CLO. This configuration fostered a remarkable synergy that allowed us to mutually enhance each other's areas of expertise. Marvelous Designer adeptly addressed inquiries within the game, animation, VFX, media entertainment sector, while CLO diligently focused on the fashion and manufacturing industry. The joyful expressions witnessed at the demo stations were a proof to the meaningful conversations in which everyone participated wholeheartedly.  


![a033d546ab9c44fc87d2a685b8bccadb](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/e9f115628645436a809e29971069a4d9/images/a033d546ab9c44fc87d2a685b8bccadb2023-08-08_SIGGRAPH_SC_184101.jpg)![8852d8be3ee04572af9e10fc6149099f](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/e9f115628645436a809e29971069a4d9/images/8852d8be3ee04572af9e10fc6149099f2023-08-08_SIGGRAPH_SC_183643.jpg)

# **2ND DAY OF SIGGRAPH: OUR MEET-UP EVENT! (August 9th 2023)**

![0d01aeea07194f4591e257bf833ad575](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/e9f115628645436a809e29971069a4d9/images/0d01aeea07194f4591e257bf833ad575e55df8830da84fd49444660da465b29d.png)

# **HOW WE MADE MARVELOUS NIGHT TOGETHER!**

We are thrilled to share the success of our networking event held during SIGGRAPH week. Heartfelt gratitude is extended to all those who joined us for the event at the nearby Nixo Patio Lounge at the E-Central Hotel. As part of the programming for the evening, we curated two engaging sessions; Miguel Ortega and Tran Ma, filmmakers at [**Half M.T Studios**](https://linktr.ee/halfmt), presented their award-winning short film, "[**The Voice in the Hollow**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_FOw3DpcB18)," which won the Jury Award at this year’s SIGGRAPH. In addition, Bryan Kim, Product Manager for Marvelous Designer, took the stage to unveil the exciting development roadmap for the upcoming year and beyond. 

![31a695a6c072469b86aef34f6d5d178d](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/e9f115628645436a809e29971069a4d9/images/31a695a6c072469b86aef34f6d5d178d2023-08-09_Reception_SC_184449.jpg)![98c9f301516940deb1a8b85219e229d2](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/e9f115628645436a809e29971069a4d9/images/98c9f301516940deb1a8b85219e229d22023-08-09_Reception_SC_184626.jpg)![43f5dbfcaa3549f3b30ced128d476fc6](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/e9f115628645436a809e29971069a4d9/images/43f5dbfcaa3549f3b30ced128d476fc62023-08-09_Reception_SC_184769.jpg)![ec5462ba9bc14551b2002e05f37de29a](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/e9f115628645436a809e29971069a4d9/images/ec5462ba9bc14551b2002e05f37de29a2023-08-09_Reception_SC_184835.jpg)

Connecting in person with our vibrant user community was a true privilege, leading to insightful conversations and invaluable feedback as well. In addition to our enriching interactions at SIGGRAPH, the meet-up event added an extra layer of engagement with our stakeholders.

We're also delighted that our message about Marvelous Designer's role in unlocking creative potential resonated. A special applause goes to the team at Half M.T Studios for their captivating presentation providing an exclusive peek behind-the-scenes utilization of Marvelous Designer.

In summary, SIGGRAPH 2023 and our meet-up event left us with an entirely positive experience. We felt all your support and gained insights into how we can enhance your experience further! We eagerly anticipate our next MARVELOUS gathering, as we continue to share our messages with you!
